payload.text: (2026-10-25, vc under hv's pen granted 2026-08-22, answering cc's plan for ST0086 WP-04 after hv saw the pipeline strip empty: 'It is now ... but not populated with any data') THE SLOT PROTOCOL IS BUILT FIRST, AS PLANNED, IN TWO PARTS. Records live under ~/.local/state/intent/estate/slots/: controller.json, lanes/<lane>.json, and requests/<ULID>/{ask,grant,deny,start,end,revoke}.json, with state as the fold and every stamp the service's. The desk maps across: READY=ask, GO=grant, START=start, END=release --result, refusals=deny or revoke; molt-vc takes control and opens lanes. Lanes are the scarce resources (cargo capacity 1 machine-wide including kovacs, bats, light, launchsvc), and a grant names every lane a run uses, with capacity checked in each; rows keep lane and gain lanes. --load-under refuses a grant above a load; --place-of keeps a hand-back's asked_at; --tag security is display only; --bytes on ask must match on start; --not-before is enforced; --hold is shown and judged by the controller. Order stays the controller's judgement. Part A (records, verbs, capacity, reader keys) lands first so the page fills; Part B (wait, watch, the prompt hook, estate init, TUI) follows. Design before code, row keys agreed with ic, each part its own heavy. molt-vc reads it before it stands; its desk stays by message until A lands and it agrees. AMENDED the same hour on molt-vc's read, all six in Part A: a heavy lane of capacity 1 that every heavy grant names, beside its resources; negligible runs ask with lane none so they show; kovacs start and release relayed by the requester with --relayed, stamps marked as relay time; the controller's revoke, or end --abandoned, frees a dead holder's capacity with a reason and kills nothing; control hold and lane hold refuse grants while they stand; only the controller's session may grant, deny, revoke, open lanes or hold, ENFORCED by session id, with --node recorded on every write. SECOND AMENDMENT, on cc and ic's objection and molt-vc's handover point: rows carry lanes alone and lane is dropped (one fact, one home); the bytes flag is --named; rows gain started_at and ended_at, null until their files exist, restoring the 'took X, ended N ago' of hv's approved mockup and named to hv; control take succeeds when there is no controller or the recorded controller's session is gone, by the page's ORPHANED test, recording the predecessor, is refused while that controller is live, and control release hands over. The page and TUI half is ic's bank under cc's /04, landing after cc's reader. THIRD AMENDMENT, on molt-vc's point that an open orphan take lets a peer take a dead desk and grant itself: an orphan take succeeds only when the caller's cross-session name, read by the tool from the caller's own Claude Code session file and never from a typed flag, equals the name controller.json recorded; any other name or a change of name needs --hv with hv's words recorded verbatim and shown on the page; a first take needs none.
